obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (enclave, FIL, or any system where CUI was found)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery ("rapidly report" as defined in 252.204-7012(a))
notify: DoD through DIBNet (requires a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Prime A, B, C subcontracts. Not triggered when only a supplier's own systems are compromised

obligation: Incident report number to the prime
trigger: The company submits a DIBNet cyber incident report
deadline: As soon as practicable after the DIBNet report
notify: Prime A, B, or C (next higher-tier contractor)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CUI subcontracts

obligation: Malicious software submission and media preservation
trigger: Malicious software isolated in connection with a reported incident, or any cyber incident reported under 252.204-7012(c)
deadline: Submit malware to DC3 as instructed; preserve images and monitoring data for at least 90 days from the report
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3); never the contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CUI subcontracts

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment identified (Section 889)
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services used as a substantial or essential component of any system, or is notified of it by a subcontractor or other source, during performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer; DoD contracts through https://dibnet.dod.mil; tell the prime the same day
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all federal channel subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky Lab covered article identified
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies a Kaspersky Lab covered article provided to the Government during performance, or is notified of it
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days of the report. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer; DoD contracts through https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the subcontract includes FAR 52.204-23 (6 of 7 federal channel purchase order templates)

obligation: FASCSA order covered article or source identified
citation: FAR 52.204-30(c)(3)-(4); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies, including through a supplier notice, that a covered article or a product from a source subject to an applicable FASCSA order was provided to the Government or used in performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days of the report. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: DoD contracting office through https://dibnet.dod.mil; other agencies: contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Prime A and Prime B subcontracts and 5 of 7 federal channel templates

obligation: Electronic parts from outside the authorized sourcing order
trigger: An electronic part for a DoD job came from a source other than the original manufacturer, its authorized suppliers, or a contractor-approved supplier, or cannot be confirmed as new and unused
deadline: Promptly, in writing; keep inspection, testing, and authentication records
notify: Contracting officer, through the prime
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CUI subcontracts
clock_starts: Purchase or identification of the part
owner: Director of Quality and Product Compliance

obligation: Counterfeit or suspect counterfeit electronic parts (counterfeit avoidance system)
trigger: Becoming aware of, or having reason to suspect, that an electronic part or assembly purchased by DoD or for delivery to DoD contains counterfeit or suspect counterfeit parts
deadline: The clause sets no fixed deadline: report on becoming aware, through Prime A; quarantine and do not return parts to the seller until determined authentic
notify: Contracting officer (through Prime A) and GIDEP
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Prime A subcontract (through paragraph (e))
owner: Director of Quality and Product Compliance

obligation: Counterfeit or suspect counterfeit items (FAR clause)
trigger: Becoming aware of or having reason to suspect that an item purchased for delivery to the Government is counterfeit or suspect counterfeit
deadline: Within 60 days: written notice to the contracting officer and a GIDEP report; keep the items until disposition instructions
notify: Contracting officer; GIDEP
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a prime flows the clause down. Not in the current subcontracts; check each new DoD purchase order
owner: Director of Quality and Product Compliance

obligation: State data breach notification (each state where affected individuals reside)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state): employees in 12 states, reseller contacts in 15 states
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; Florida rows below are the worked example
clock_starts: Each state's own trigger (often discovery or determination of the breach)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause under 501.171(3)(a); it applies only to this notice)
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information of Florida residents is involved

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (no extension)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company (worked example, inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example payroll or the portal vendor) has a breach
deadline: The vendor must notify the company within 10 days of determining the breach
notify: The company (Security Manager and General Counsel)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendor duty; the company's own clock starts when it learns of the breach

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Business email compromise and payment fraud report
trigger: A supplier or company mailbox is used to request a bank change or payment, whether or not money moved
deadline: Voluntary; file as soon as possible and call the bank fraud desk at once to try to recall any payment
notify: FBI IC3 (www.ic3.gov); company bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary)

obligation: Reseller contract incident notice
citation: Reseller agreements (3 national resellers) and portal terms (contract)
trigger: Security incident affecting reseller data or the Partner Commerce Platform
deadline: 72 hours from confirmation, per the agreements
notify: Affected resellers' security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident, including ransomware, payment fraud, and supplier compromise
deadline: Call the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors ($500,000 retention)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Public company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
notify: SEC / investors (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity (as defined in the final rule)
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final
